samples.question: The image shows two separate cords of the same dark teal ink, one in each of two far-apart corners of the picture, with clear background between them. Each cord is a single unbranched stroke of constant thickness folded into flat back-and-forth switchbacks: it never branches, never crosses itself and never touches itself or the other cord. Exactly two small square beads are printed on each cord. One cord carries both orange beads and the other cord carries both purple beads; no cord carries beads of two colours. For each cord, measure the separation between its two beads by travelling along that cord's own ink from one bead to the other, following every fold; a straight jump across background, or across a neighbouring fold, is never a legal step. The two straight-line bead separations are deliberately built to be almost equal, so the straight-line gap tells you nothing: only the distances measured along the cords differ. Both cords must be inspected, since the answer is a comparison between them. All gray shapes anywhere in the image are decoration and mean nothing. Which bead pair is farther apart measured along its own cord? Answer orange or purple.
